questions.definition: The maximum amount of data transmitted over an internet connection in a given amount of time.
questions.clue: Higher values allow more data to be sent per second.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is a measure of data transfer capacity. It is often measured in bits per second, such as Mbps or Gbps.

questions.definition: A transmission method where data is transmitted in both directions at the same time.
questions.clue: Both devices can send and receive simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication is efficient because both ends can transmit at once, such as during a telephone call.

questions.definition: A transmission method where data is transmitted in both directions, but only one direction at a time.
questions.clue: Both directions are possible, but not simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Half-duplex allows two-way communication, but devices must take turns transmitting, such as with walkie-talkies.

questions.definition: A very large global network that allows users to access the World Wide Web and other services.
questions.explanation: The internet connects many networks globally. The World Wide Web is one service that runs on the internet.

questions.definition: The time taken for data to travel between its source and destination, usually measured in milliseconds.
questions.explanation: High latency can make online activities feel slow, especially video calls, gaming, or satellite internet connections.

questions.definition: A section of a data packet that contains information about the packet and its destination.
questions.explanation: A packet header helps network devices route the packet correctly and may include source, destination, and sequence information.

questions.definition: A method of transmitting data packets across a network where each packet can take an individual route.
questions.clue: Packets may arrive out of order.
questions.explanation: Packet switching splits data into packets. Each packet is routed independently and reassembled at the destination.

questions.definition: A small unit of data sent across a network.
questions.explanation: Large messages are split into packets for transmission, making network communication more reliable and efficient.

questions.definition: A transmission method where data is transmitted in a single direction only.
questions.explanation: Simplex transmission allows data to flow from sender to receiver only, with no return communication on the same channel.

questions.definition: A type of transmission medium that uses the USB standard to transmit data.
questions.clue: A physical cable for connecting devices.
questions.explanation: USB cables can transfer data and may also provide power between devices.

questions.definition: Using a USB cable plugged into a USB port to transfer data from one device to another.
questions.clue: A cable and port working together.
questions.explanation: A USB connection allows devices such as phones, keyboards, and storage drives to communicate with a computer.

questions.definition: A device that plugs into a USB port on a computer.
questions.clue: Examples include keyboards and flash drives.
questions.explanation: USB devices use the USB standard to communicate with a host device such as a computer.

questions.definition: A socket on a device or computer that enables a USB cable or device to be inserted.
questions.explanation: A USB port provides the connection point for USB devices and cables.

questions.definition: An industry standard used to transmit data between devices.
questions.explanation: USB defines how devices connect, communicate, and sometimes receive power.

questions.definition: An error detection method that uses acknowledgement and timeout to check whether data arrived correctly.
questions.explanation: If an acknowledgement is not received before timeout, the sender retransmits the data.

questions.definition: An error detection method for data entry where a calculated value is used to check whether entered data is correct.
questions.clue: Often used in barcodes or account numbers.
questions.explanation: A check digit is calculated from the original digits. If the recalculated value does not match, an error may have occurred.

questions.definition: An error detection method that performs a calculation on data to create a checksum value for comparison after transmission.
questions.explanation: The sender and receiver compare checksum values. If they differ, the data may have been corrupted.

questions.definition: An error detection method that sends a copy of transmitted data back to the sender for comparison.
questions.explanation: The sender compares the returned data with the original. Differences suggest an error occurred during transmission.

questions.definition: An error detection method that adds an additional bit to each byte to create an odd or even sum.
questions.explanation: A parity bit helps detect some errors by checking whether the number of 1s is odd or even as expected.

questions.definition: A type of encryption that uses two different keys to encrypt and decrypt data.
questions.explanation: Asymmetric encryption uses a public key and a private key. What one key encrypts, the paired key can decrypt.

questions.definition: The name given to data after encryption.
questions.explanation: Cipher text is scrambled data produced by encryption. It should not reveal the original message without decryption.

questions.definition: A method of securing data for storage or transmission by scrambling it using an encryption key.
questions.clue: Makes data meaningless without a key.
questions.explanation: Encryption protects confidentiality by converting plain text into cipher text.

questions.definition: The name given to data before encryption.
questions.explanation: Plain text is the original readable message before it is encrypted.

questions.definition: A type of encryption that uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt data.
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption can be fast, but the shared key must be exchanged securely.

questions.definition: The actual data that the user is sending to the receiver.
questions.clue: The useful data inside a packet.
questions.explanation: The payload is the main content of a packet, separate from control information such as headers and trailers.

questions.definition: A section of a data packet that contains information about error checking methods that may be used.
questions.clue: Found at the end of a packet.
questions.explanation: A trailer may contain error-checking data so the receiver can detect whether the packet was corrupted.

questions.definition: A system for connecting devices to form a local area network using cables.
questions.explanation: Ethernet is commonly used in LANs because it provides reliable wired data transmission.

questions.definition: A network component that examines a data packet to obtain its destination address and forwards it to that address.
questions.explanation: Routers choose where packets should go next so data can travel across networks to its destination.

questions.definition: Computers and devices joined together using cables or wireless technology.
questions.explanation: Networks allow devices to share data, printers, internet connections, and other resources.

questions.definition: The unique address given to a device when it is connected to a network.
questions.clue: Used to identify devices on a network.
questions.explanation: An IP address helps data packets reach the correct device on a network.

questions.definition: A disadvantage of parallel transmission where signals arrive at different times because wires have slightly different properties.
questions.explanation: Skew can cause timing problems in parallel transmission because each signal may travel at a slightly different speed.

questions.definition: The shared key in asymmetric cryptography that can be used with a matching private key.
questions.explanation: A public key can be distributed openly. Data encrypted with a public key can only be decrypted with its paired private key.

questions.definition: The key in asymmetric cryptography that should not be shared with anyone.
questions.explanation: A private key must be protected. It can decrypt data encrypted with the matching public key and can be used for digital signatures.
